summary: Keisuke Fujii is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1986), where he held posts from 1982 to 2018, later serving as a visiting professor at Tokyo University of the Arts.

Keith Dowman works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under numerous traditional teachers, including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

Keiya Noguchi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Kyoto University (~1978–1985). He held appointments at Shuchiin University as lecturer (~1993–1998) and professor (~2003), and at Taisho University (attested 1995 and 2017).

Kelsang Gyatso was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Chambaling, Tashi Lhunpo, Ngamring Chöde, and Sera monasteries under Trijang Rinpoche. He taught at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre (1977) and founded the New Kadampa Tradition (1991).

Kelsey Alise Seymour specializes in Sinology and Japanology. She completed her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair (attested 2018) and was a Visiting Predoctoral Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (2017–2018).
Kemo Jin worked in Indology, Sinology, and linguistics. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (1941–1945) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University from 1948.

Ken McLeod works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an M.Sc. at the University of British Columbia, studied under traditional teachers including Kalu Rinpoche, taught at Kagyu Dongak Chuling (~1985–1990), and founded Unfettered Mind in 1990.

Kendall Marchman specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Florida (2008–2015), studying under Mario Poceski, and held assistant professorships at Young Harris College (2014–2018) and the University of Georgia (2018).

Kendall Wayne Folkert was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Western Michigan University, the University of Göttingen under Carsten Colpe, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, later serving as an associate professor at Central Michigan University (~1974–1985).

Kengo Harimoto works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Nagasaki, Kyushu, and Pennsylvania (PhD under Wilhelm Halbfass). He has held positions at Hamburg, Temple, Leiden, Groningen, Mahidol, and Naples "L'Orientale."

Kenichi Kuranishi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held positions as associate professor at Taisho University (attested 2013–2026) and as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Kenji Ishii is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1983) and held a post at Kokugakuin University around 1992.
Kenji Kinugawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1972–1980) under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.

Kenji Matsuo specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1975–1984, PhD student in 2023) and held a post at Yamagata University (~1989–2020).
Kenji Shimada was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1938–1941) and later worked there as a researcher (~1950–1981).

Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop and with Diwakar Acharya and Yuko Yokochi. He held a fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II (2019–2021) and a post at Toyo University (attested 2024).
Kenji Watanabe specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jozef Deleu and held a post at the University of Tokyo around 1978.
Kenjiu Kasawara was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879 under Friedrich Max Müller (1879–1882) and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.
Kenjuro Yanagida was a philosopher who studied at Yokohama National University and under Kitaro Nishida (~1922–1925). He held a post at Hirosaki University (~1949–1950).
Kenkai Naganuma was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He held appointments at Kyushu University (~1926–1944) and Kurume University (~1950).
